brief: ING's September US jobs report note builds a causal chain: non-farm payrolls rose just 29k against a 90k consensus, with 60k of prior-month downward revisions, while the unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, driven not by layoffs but by workers returning to the labour force (participation up to 61.8% from 61.6%, a 485k increase). Wage growth slowed to 3% y/y from 3.1%, which ING reads as showing no inflation pressure from the jobs market. Combined with recent dovish comments from Fed officials John Williams and Philip Jefferson, this pushes the Fed toward holding rates in October. Only a hot September CPI print, due 14 October, would make that meeting live. ING's house call remains a December hike, and it still views market pricing of three to four further hikes as too aggressive. By sector, manufacturing extended a fourth straight monthly gain (72k added year to date) and construction rose on data centre linked activity, while services (information, financial, professional services, government) all shed jobs. A falling quits rate points to further wage softening ahead.
